resource.description:
RRF funding aims to fill gaps in immediate working capital for small businesses and nonprofits (including cultural organizations) until they can resume more normal operations.  Recipients may or may not have applied for additional funding through Small Business Administration (SBA) loans and other federal disaster relief funding sources.  Using $2 million of the City’s share of Food and Beverage Tax funds that the Bloomington Common Council approved for expenditure April 7, plus $500,000 of additional support approved by the Bloomington Urban Enterprise Association on April 8, the City is providing these immediate loans of up to $50,000 each to sustain area businesses in the short term and foster the regional economy.

An advisory committee was appointed by the City of Bloomington to review applications and make recommendations for funding. This committee includes representatives from banking, financial services, and community organizations.  Additionally, applicants may seek support on their application by contacting the City of Bloomington at economicvitality@bloomington.in.gov.

For more information about this and other Recover Forward efforts, see: https://bloomington.in.gov/recoverforward

resource.name: Fire Incident Responses
resource.description: Fire Department responses to calls for service
columns_description: The fire apparatus that responded to the call. The values are entered manually.
The plain language version of the "unit" field; how Fire Department staff refer to the apparatus that responded to the call.

Incident number: System-generated unique identifier assigned to a response to a call for service. The format is 'YY-#######' where YY= last two digits of the 'notif_datetime' field's year; #######= the unique sequence number associated with the incident. For example, the first incident recorded in 2021 would have an inci_no of '21-0000001'.
Incident type: A 3-digit code defined by the National Fire Incident Reporting System that automatically correlates to the 'inci_desc' field
Incident description: The description of the type of incident to which crews responded. The descriptions are correlated with the field 'inci_type'.
Response code: Manually entered codes that define the type of response as '1' for 'emergent', '2' for 'non-emergent', and 'c' if the call was canceled.
Response description: Plain language description of the three codes associated with the type of response -  '1' for 'emergent', '2' for 'non-emergent', and 'c' if the call was canceled.
Alarm date-time: Dispatch system-generated timestamp of when dispatch received the call for service. The validity of this field is in question as it equals 'notif_datetime' 100% of the time.

Notification date-time: Dispatch system-generated timestamp that contains the date and time when dispatch notified the Fire Department of the incident. This timestamp starts the clock for all of the time-based metrics for the department.
Roll date-time: How generated? Timestamp of when the front tires of the fire apparatus are out of the station doors.
Arrival date-time: How generated? Timestamp of when the fire apparatus is at a complete stop at the incident destination.
Address type: Values are automatically generated when 'address' is entered. Values are either '1' or '2'. The meaning of these values is unknown.
Address: Dispatch system-generated exact address for the location of the incident.
Address 2: Additional information like an apartment number generated by the dispatch system needed to find the exact location of the incident.

Cross-street: Dispatch system-generated information about the location of the incident when the incident is not a street address. This field is typically used when responding to a motor vehicle crash site.

Rural directions: Dispatch system-generated information about the location of the incident when the incident is not a street address. This field is typically used when responding to a remote or undeveloped location. Values could be like 'Mile marker ## on southbound I69'.
City: Dispatch system-generated city in which the incident occurs.
State: Dispatch system-generated state in which the incident occurs.
Zipcode: Dispatch system-generated zipcode in which the incident occurs.
Fire: Manually-entered information indicating that the call for service was to respond to a fire.
Medical: Manually-entered information indicating that the call for service was to respond to a medical situation that may or may not be associated with a fire..
Rescue: Manually-entered information indicating that the call for service was to respond to a request for rescue that may or may not be associated with a fire.
Other: Fire: Manually-entered information indicating that the call for service was to respond to a request that was something other than a fire, a medical need, or a rescue.
Response time in minutes: Calculated field that subtracts the value in 'notif_datetime' from the value in 'arv_datetime' and rounds to the nearest whole minute.
Fire Department Identifier: The federal identification number associated with the Bloomington Fire Department. This field will always have the value '53003'.

resource.name: HAA5 LRAA Data
resource.description: Two disinfectant byproducts (DBPs), Total Trihalomethanes (TTHMs) and Haloacedic Acids (HAA5s) are regulated by the Safe Drinking Water Act through the Stage 2 Disinfectant Byproduct Rule. The City of Bloomington Utilities collects samples for DBPs monthly at 8 testing locations throughout the distribution system and follows a quarterly compliance schedule. Compliance is calculated on a Locational Running Annual Average (LRAA). The Maximum Contaminant Levels are 80 µg/l for TTHMs and 60 µg/l for HAA5s. Micrograms per liter (µg/l) is equal to parts per billion (ppb). One part per billion is roughly equal to a teaspoon of water in an Olympic-size swimming pool.

resource.description: This map data layer represents the former Areas Intended for Annexation for the City of Bloomington, Indiana, also known as the AIFA. This area was establish by an inter-local agreement between the City of Bloomington and Monroe County Government in 1996 to establish an area outside the City limits where the City planned to annex. The AIFA replaced the 2 Mile Fringe boundary as the area that the City retained planning jurisdiction outside the City incorporated boundary. This agreement has expired in 2013 and AIFA area that had not been annexed by the City returned to Monroe County planning jurisdiction.

resource.name: City of Bloomington Sars CoV-2 (COVID-19) Wastewater Monitoring
resource.description:
The City of Bloomington Utilities (CBU) in cooperation with the Indiana Finance Authority is participating in a monitoring program which tests wastewater for coronavirus. From August through December of 2020, wastewater professionals from CBU collected samples three times each week at eight sites across Bloomington, including each of the two wastewater treatment plants. Throughout 2021 samples have been collected from the two wastewater treatment plants. Testing of those samples is conducted by multiple private, independent laboratories in an effort to gauge viral prevalence in the community. 

More information about this process can be found in the Indiana Wastewater Monitoring Report 2020 at: 

https://data.bloomington.in.gov/dataset/cd07435a-adae-4ba6-b671-2b711227131d/resource/22b67271-e2d4-4789-af7d-4fc7a586071c/download/indiana-wastewater-monitoring-report-2020_bclear.pdf
